question.problem: Suppose that $X$ and $Y$ are independent random variables such that $X∼N(-5,16)$ and $Y∼N(1,1).$ Find the distribution of the random variable $W=-X+3Y.$
question.worked_solution:
Recall that if ${X}_{1}$ and ${X}_{2}$ are independent random variables, where ${X}_{1}∼N({\mu }_{1},{\sigma }_{1}^{2})$ and ${X}_{2}∼N({\mu }_{2},{\sigma }_{2}^{2}),$ and $a$ and $b$ are constants, then 

$$
a{X}_{1}+b{X}_{2}∼N(a{\mu }_{1}+b{\mu }_{2},{a}^{2}{\sigma }_{1}^{2}+{b}^{2}{\sigma }_{2}^{2}).
$$

Since $X$ and $Y$ are independent, we have 

$$
\begin{aligned}W=-X+3Y & ∼N(-(-5)+3\cdot 1,(-1)^{2}\cdot 16+(3)^{2}\cdot 1) \\  & ∼N(8,25).\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $Y∼N(8,25).$
